scope: Strict-radius midpoints give actual same-source segments in a proper metric space; actual cone midpoints give angular midpoints; original finite-dimensional local geometry gives compact pi-geodesic actual completed directions at the same point.
errata: The retained AKP erratum was reread and has no correction to Lemma2.13; existing source qualifications reused, without fresh external retrieval or a general absence-of-errata claim.
source_normalization: Formal comparison parameter1 means curvature -1. Angular distances are radians with the strict threshold dist<pi; the actual cone metric uses min(pi,dist).
source_scope_translation: The generic dyadic and cone-segment adapters explicitly assume ProperSpace, stronger than the source completeness needed for dyadic limits. Compact actual directions supply this hypothesis in the final source-facing consumers. Finite Hausdorff bound supplies proved covering compactness; no equivalence with source linear dimension is assumed.
proof_route: Alternate noncircular route: coarse local covering gives compact actual directions, the preceding full-sequence actual tangent blowup and same-target segment closure give tangent geodesicity, exact cone midpoint recovery gives angular midpoints, and restricted dyadic completion gives segments only below pi. The direct KLP6.5 moving-midpoint argument and its sharp packing bound are not claimed.
empty_base_convention: Option-based EuclideanCone adjoins a tip even for an empty base; no angular point is manufactured from that tip. Actual singleton source has empty completed directions and a singleton tangent.
